Syllabus Tag: GS3 › Environment › Conservation, environmental pollution and degradation, environmental impact assessment › Air pollution — GRAP, CAQM
CA Topic / Headline: Delhi winter pollution curbs kick in from Nov 1: non-Delhi non-BS-VI vehicles barred, no fuel without valid PUC; CPCB orders closure of NCR units that have not ordered APCDs within five days; CAQM PM limit 50 mg/Nm3 for 17 highly polluting categories.
Prelims Recall (CSE 2027):
• CAQM PM emission limit: 50 mg/Nm3 for 17 highly polluting industry categories, applicable from October 1.
• APCDs are filtration and emission-control systems fitted to industrial exhaust stacks; bag filters are one type.
• Delhi curbs: non-Delhi non-BS-VI vehicles barred from Nov 1 to Jan 31; no fuel without valid PUC certificate.
• Rain pulled Delhi average AQI down to 60 on Friday, per the IITM-maintained network.
Mains Recall (CSE 2027):
• [Issue] Several NCR units had not ordered new APCDs or obtained adequacy assessment reports, prompting CPCB closure directions.
• [Intro data] CPCB letter of October 30 asked Delhi PCC and Haryana, U.P., Rajasthan boards to issue show-cause notices.
• [Way forward] Pair vehicle curbs with continuous stack monitoring, time-bound APCD retrofits and region-wide enforcement across NCR States.
• [Counterpoint] Seasonal bans hurt gig workers and border traffic while year-round sources keep emitting.

Syllabus Tag: GS3 › Science & Technology › IT, space, computers, robotics, nanotechnology, biotechnology, intellectual property rights › NavIC — NVS series
CA Topic / Headline: GSLV-F18 places NVS-03 in orbit (apogee 38,080 km vs planned 37,247 km), restoring NavIC to its minimum four-satellite configuration; ISRO flew it with pyro valves pre-opened after the NVS-02 failure.
Prelims Recall (CSE 2027):
• NVS-03 launched on GSLV-F18 from Sriharikota on October 30.
• NavIC needs at least four satellites for standalone positioning; NVS-03 restored that minimum.
• NVS-03 has a 12-year mission life and adds the L1 band (V&R).
• Last atomic clock aboard IRNSS-1F stopped working in March.
Mains Recall (CSE 2027):
• [Issue] NVS-02 (2025) failed because the drive signal did not reach the oxidiser pyro valve.
• [Issue] Indigenous clocks face procurement challenges; ISRO proposes up to five clocks per satellite.
• [Way forward] Launch NVS-04 and NVS-05 quickly, mandate NavIC chipsets and build clock supply chains.
• [Intro data] Original IRNSS satellites were launched between 2013 and 2018.

Syllabus Tag: GS3 › Internal Security › Communication networks, media and social networking, cyber security, money-laundering › Content blocking — Sec 69A, 79(3)(b), IT Rules
CA Topic / Headline: MeitY advisories of October 8 and 10 amid anti-CEC protests drive a wave of post and account blocking on Meta and X; amended IT Rules cut takedown time to three hours from 36; users face 60-90 day grievance delays.
Prelims Recall (CSE 2027):
• Section 69A, IT Act, 2000: Centre may block online content on sovereignty, security, public order grounds.
• Section 79(3)(b): safe-harbour can lapse if an intermediary fails to act on lawful notice.
• Rule 3(1)(d), IT Rules 2021: takedown within three hours of court order or authorised intimation.
• Grievance Appellate Committee hears appeals against platform grievance officers’ decisions.
Mains Recall (CSE 2027):
• [Issue] Platform-level removals under community standards leave users without constitutional-court remedy, per advocate Rishav Ranjan.
• [Intro data] Delhi Police issued about 300 takedown requests in three months, most acted upon (V&R).
• [Way forward] Publish reasoned orders, add notice and hearing, and set time-bound GAC review.
• [Counterpoint] Rapid removal limits deepfakes and incitement during volatile protests.

Syllabus Tag: GS3 › Economy › Infrastructure: energy, ports, roads, airports, railways › Ethanol blending — E20, E100, flex-fuel
CA Topic / Headline: MoRTH amends Central Motor Vehicles Rules, 1989 to include E100 alongside E85, paving way for flex-fuel vehicle homologation; existing vehicles need not switch; India hit E20 in 2025, five years early.
Prelims Recall (CSE 2027):
• E100 is fuel with 100% ethanol; usable only in vehicles designed for it.
• India achieved E20 in 2025, five years ahead of the 2030 deadline under National Policy on Biofuels, 2018.
• From April 2026, all BS-VI vehicles must meet E20 emission standards.
• Homologation is official certification by agencies such as ARAI before type approval.
Mains Recall (CSE 2027):
• [Issue] Ethanol’s lower energy density lowers mileage; government estimates about 5% decline.
• [Issue] Large-scale ethanol needs land and water and competes with food crops.
• [Counterpoint] Experts warn blending distracts from electrification, a clearer path to deep emission cuts.
• [Way forward] Diversify to second-generation feedstock, track lifecycle emissions and build flex-fuel dispensing.

CA Topic / Headline: Explainer on Legislative Councils after the 28-seat Council polls: Article 169 creation or abolition, Article 171 composition, limited powers (delay a bill by four months) and Second ARC’s ‘council of local governments’ idea.
Prelims Recall (CSE 2027):
• Article 168: six States have Councils — Maharashtra, Uttar Pradesh, Bihar, Andhra Pradesh, Telangana and Karnataka.
• Article 169: Parliament, by ordinary law, may create or abolish a Council if the Assembly passes a resolution by two-thirds majority.
• Article 171: at most one-third of Assembly strength, minimum 40; one-third elected by local bodies and one-third by MLAs; one-sixth nominated.
• Article 172: not subject to dissolution; members’ term six years, one-third retiring every two years.
• Council can delay an Assembly-passed bill for a maximum of four months.

• [Judgment] Second ARC (2007): make Councils ‘councils of local governments’ elected solely by local-body representatives.
• [Intro data] 1935 Act introduced bicameral legislatures in six provinces; Constituent Assembly debated Councils as a check on hasty legislation.
• [Counterpoint] Critics call Councils an unnecessary exchequer burden and object that key aspects are left to ordinary law; supporters cite their revising role.

Syllabus Tag: GS3 › Science & Technology › IT, space, computers, robotics, nanotechnology, biotechnology, intellectual property rights › Data protection — DPDP Act, AI training
CA Topic / Headline: Op-ed: DPDP Act (2023; Rules notified November 2025) does not cover publicly available or inferred data, creates no sensitive-data category and is silent on AI training; consent provisions apply only from 2027 and users have no right to object.
Prelims Recall (CSE 2027):
• DPDP Act passed in 2023; DPDP Rules notified in November 2025; implementation is phased.
• Substantive provisions take full effect in May 2027; consent and safety provisions effective only in 2027.
• Right to privacy was upheld by the Supreme Court in 2017.
• IT Act, 2000 and 2011 Rules covered ‘sensitive personal data’, with criminal penalty capped at three years’ imprisonment or ₹5 lakh fine.
• DPDP right to erasure applies only to data given with consent; research, archival and statistical processing is exempt.
Mains Recall (CSE 2027):
• [Issue] DPDP Act excludes publicly available data and inferred data (emotions, mobility, behaviour), and buckets all personal data together with no sensitive category.
• [Issue] AI models can regurgitate training data; “anonymised” datasets can be used to extract personal details and profile individuals.
• [Way forward] Apply the Act to AI training data, give a right to object, strengthen erasure, clarify the research exemption and create a sensitive-data category.
• [Counterpoint] Indiscriminate regulation risks inhibiting innovation; Meta allows EU users an AI-training opt-out but Indians have none.

Prelims Recall (CSE 2027):
• SUMP planned at 11.2 GW in Upper Siang, Arunachal Pradesh, as a buffer against China’s 60-GW dam on the Yarlung Tsangpo.
• The Yarlung Tsangpo becomes the Brahmaputra in India; the Tibet dam has five cascading stations over a 2,000-metre fall.
• China has agreed only to share hydrological data on humanitarian grounds during emergencies.

Mains Recall (CSE 2027):
• [Issue] Security forces guard survey teams and the State Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act is used against activists, validating fears of land grab.
• [Issue] China declines to share engineering details; downstream flow is mostly monsoon and tributary-fed, limiting Chinese control but not near-border risks.
• [Way forward] Diplomacy for data-sharing, plus compliance with all laws and protections, and consent of Adi communities.
• [Ethics] The state cannot protect the nation’s needs by antagonising the nation’s people.

Syllabus Tag: GS2 › International Relations › Effect of policies and politics of developed and developing countries on India's interests; Indian diaspora › India-US — Pannun civil suit against Doval and Goel
CA Topic / Headline: A US court allowed Khalistani separatist Gurpatwant Singh Pannun to serve his civil suit on NSA Ajit Doval and ex-RAW chief Samant Goel via Indian judicial channels after State Department certification; India calls it frivolous. Why it matters: sovereign immunity, extradition and legal assistance in India-US ties (GS2 IR).
Prelims Recall (CSE 2027):
• Extradition Act, 1962 is the legislative basis for extradition from India, which also needs a treaty, agreement or arrangement. https://www.mea.gov.in/extradition-from-india
• India-US Extradition Treaty was signed on 25 June 1997 and entered into force on 21 July 1999. https://www.state.gov/12873
• India is party to the Hague Service Convention and objects to Article 10 service by postal channels. https://travel.state.gov/content/travel/en/legal/Judicial-Assistance-Country-Information/India.html
• US Foreign Sovereign Immunities Act, 1976: foreign states are immune from US courts except as provided in sections 1605 to 1607. https://www.congress.gov/crs-product/LSB11363
• MEA is India's Central Authority for extradition requests; Letters Rogatory and MLAT requests are separate channels for legal assistance. https://static.pib.gov.in/WriteReadData/userfiles/ISII_ComprehensiveGuidelinesMutualLegalAssistance_17122019.pdf
Mains Recall (CSE 2027):
• [Provision] India-US treaty bars extradition for political offences (Article 4) and does not allow nationality as a ground for refusal (Article 3). https://www.state.gov/wp-content/uploads/2019/02/12873-India-Law-Enforcement-Extradition-6.25.1997.pdf
• [Provision] FSIA exceptions to immunity include waiver, commercial activity in the US and tortious acts causing harm in the US. https://www.congress.gov/crs_external_products/LSB/HTML/LSB11363.html
• [Judgment] Halkbank (US Supreme Court): FSIA gives no immunity from criminal prosecution, so civil and criminal immunity routes differ. https://www.congress.gov/crs-product/LSB10967
• [Counterpoint] Extradition Act, 1962 places no bar on extraditing Indian nationals, so India's own practice cuts both ways. https://meacms.mea.gov.in/extradition-from-india.htm
• [Way forward] Contest jurisdiction on sovereign-immunity grounds and route evidence requests through treaty-based legal assistance rather than public confrontation. https://static.pib.gov.in/WriteReadData/userfiles/ISII_ComprehensiveGuidelinesMutualLegalAssistance_17122019.pdf

• [Counterpoint] Implementation lags: by December 2023, Rs 9,650 crore was released to NCAP cities but about Rs 5,835 crore utilised. https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleaseIframePage.aspx?PRID=1989207

Syllabus Tag: GS3 › Economy › Infrastructure: energy, ports, roads, airports, railways › Inland waterways — Namo Yamuna River Cruise
CA Topic / Headline: Sarbananda Sonowal and Delhi CM Rekha Gupta launched the 'Namo Yamuna River Cruise Service': a 30-passenger electric cruise from Sonia Vihar to Jagatpur, 6 km, 35-45 minutes, proposed fare Rs 500 plus Rs 50 entry fee. Why it matters: inland-waterway tourism on NW-110 (Yamuna) under the National Waterways framework (GS3 Infrastructure).
Prelims Recall (CSE 2027):
• National Waterways Act, 2016 declared 111 inland waterways (including 5 earlier ones) as National Waterways across 24 states. https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=1847361&reg=48&lang=2
• National Waterway 110 is the Yamuna: 1,080 km across Delhi, Haryana and Uttar Pradesh. https://www.pib.gov.in/pressrelesedetailm.aspx?prid=1605385&reg=48&lang=2
• NW-1 is the Ganga-Bhagirathi-Hooghly system from Haldia to Allahabad (1,620 km), the longest of the five original waterways. https://www.pib.gov.in/pressrelesedetailm.aspx?prid=1605385&reg=48&lang=2
• Inland Waterways Authority of India was constituted in 1985 to augment waterway transport capacity. https://iwai.gov.in/sites/default/files/2024-07/6991446056volume_3_consolidated_eia_main_vol.pdf
• Jal Marg Vikas Project on NW-1 (Haldia to Varanasi) is World Bank-assisted and costs Rs 5,369.18 crore. https://www.pib.gov.in/pressrelesedetailm.aspx?prid=1605385&reg=48&lang=2
Mains Recall (CSE 2027):
• [Provision] National Waterways Act, 2016 provides for declaring inland waterways as national waterways and regulating and developing them for shipping and navigation. https://www.indiacode.nic.in/bitstream/123456789/2159/1/A2016-17.pdf
• [Scheme] JMVP fairway works target least available depth of 3.0 m (Haldia-Barh), 2.5 m (Barh-Ghazipur) and 2.2 m (Ghazipur-Varanasi). https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleseDetailm.aspx?PRID=1943652&reg=3&lang=2
• [Data] Operational national waterways carried about 72.31 million tonnes per annum of cargo (March 2020). https://www.pib.gov.in/pressrelesedetailm.aspx?prid=1605385&reg=48&lang=2
• [Counterpoint] Viability is limited: only 26 of 111 waterways passed techno-economic feasibility for cargo or passenger movement, so cruises will not scale everywhere. https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=1847361&reg=48&lang=2
• [Way forward] Maintain least available depth through fairway works and match vessel draught to river depth, as JMVP does on NW-1. https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleseDetailm.aspx?PRID=1943652&reg=3&lang=2

Syllabus Tag: GS2 › Polity › Salient features of the Representation of People's Act › Electoral rolls — Form 7 deletions in Mustafabad
CA Topic / Headline: 796 Form 7 applications to delete voters, filed by 20 BJP-appointed BLAs in Delhi's Mustafabad, were concentrated on 25 of 294 booths and all targeted Muslim electors, The Hindu found. Why it matters: roll integrity, Article 324 powers and Representation of the People Act, 1950 revision safeguards (GS2 Polity).
Prelims Recall (CSE 2027):
• Article 324(1): Election Commission superintends, directs and controls electoral rolls and elections to Parliament, State legislatures, and the offices of President and Vice-President. https://www.constitutionofindia.net/articles/article-324-superintendence-direction-and-control-of-elections-to-be-vested-in-an-election-commission/
• RP Act, 1950 section 21: rolls are prepared by a qualifying date and revised before general elections and bye-elections. https://prsindia.org/files/bills_acts/bills_parliament/2006/bill105_20070926105_representatiin_of_people_act_1950.pdf
• Each State has a Chief Electoral Officer (RP Act, 1950 section 13A) who supervises preparation, revision and correction of rolls. https://upload.indiacode.nic.in/showfile?actid=AC_CEN_3_20_00016_195043_1517807321506&filename=03_representation_of_the_people_act%2C_1950.pdf&type=actfile
• Article 324(2): the Election Commission comprises the Chief Election Commissioner and other Commissioners the President fixes, appointed subject to parliamentary law. https://www.constitutionofindia.net/articles/article-324-superintendence-direction-and-control-of-elections-to-be-vested-in-an-election-commission/
• Article 327 lets Parliament legislate on elections, expressly subject to the Constitution, including Article 324. https://www.eci.gov.in/eci/public/api/document?id=17370
Mains Recall (CSE 2027):
• [Provision] Section 21(3) RP Act, 1950 lets the Commission, for recorded reasons, order a special revision of any constituency or part of it. https://prsindia.org/files/bills_acts/bills_parliament/2006/bill105_20070926105_representatiin_of_people_act_1950.pdf
• [Judgment] Supreme Court: Article 324 operates in areas left unoccupied by legislation; its words are of the broadest amplitude. https://www.eci.gov.in/eci/public/api/document?id=17433
• [Judgment] 2026 INSC 564 (SIR): Articles 324 and 327 are complementary, and section 21(3) RP Act supplies statutory authority for special revision. https://www.eci.gov.in/eci/public/api/document?id=17370
• [Counterpoint] Plenary power is not unbounded: the Commission cannot defy an express statutory prohibition, so deletions must stay within RP Act rules. https://www.eci.gov.in/eci/public/api/document?id=17370
• [Way forward] Strengthen CEO and DEO supervision and record reasons for revisions; the existing roll stays in force until a special revision finishes. https://prsindia.org/files/bills_acts/bills_parliament/2006/bill105_20070926105_representatiin_of_people_act_1950.pdf

CA Topic / Headline: PLFS/Time Use Survey data finds most of the surge in women's employment went to agriculture: rural women in crop and animal production rose from 54 million to over 100 million; average weekly hours fell for every group between 2017-18 and 2025. Why it matters: female participation versus job quality (GS3 Inclusive growth).
Prelims Recall (CSE 2027):
• PLFS was launched by NSO in April 2017; LFPR is the share of the labour force in the population, WPR the employed share. https://www.mospi.gov.in/sites/default/files/press_release/Press_note_AR_PLFS_2023_24_22092024.pdf
• From 2025 the PLFS survey period moved from July-June to the January-December calendar year. https://www.mospi.gov.in/uploads/publications_reports/publications_reports1780040415321_0624fb13-fb47-40bc-b470-7c7e9635c3ef_PLFS_2025_F_REV_29052026.pdf
• Usual status (ps+ss) classifies activity over the preceding 365 days, combining principal and subsidiary status. https://www.mospi.gov.in/sites/default/files/publication_reports/PLFS%20Monthly%20Bulletin%20June%202025.pdf

Mains Recall (CSE 2027):
• [Data] Female WPR (usual status, 15+) rose from 22.0% in 2017-18 to 40.3% in 2023-24. https://www.mospi.gov.in/sites/default/files/press_release/Press_note_AR_PLFS_2023_24_22092024.pdf
• [Counterpoint] Agriculture's employment share eased only from 44.8% (2024) to 43.0% (2025) and it remains the largest employer. https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2246009&lang=1&reg=3

• [Way forward] Expand women's regular and manufacturing jobs; PLFS 2025 shows manufacturing's worker share rising as agriculture's falls. https://www.mospi.gov.in/uploads/latestReleases/latest_release_1774607827733_3e8964a9-268b-4cc9-ad65-cfc8a9e32f08_Press_note_AR_PLFS_2025_23032025_V2.1_26032026_final.pdf

Syllabus Tag: GS2 › Social Justice › Welfare schemes for vulnerable sections; mechanisms, laws, institutions and bodies for their protection › OBC creamy layer — Rohith Nathan (2026)
CA Topic / Headline: An op-ed notes that in Rohith Nathan (2026) the Supreme Court rejected use of a 2004 'clarification' to exclude OBC civil-services candidates by parental salary alone; the government used it from around 2015. Why it matters: creamy-layer criteria, Indra Sawhney and OBC reservation (GS2 Social Justice).
Prelims Recall (CSE 2027):
• Indra Sawhney v Union of India (16 November 1992) upheld 27% OBC reservation under Article 16(4), set a 50% ceiling and mandated creamy-layer exclusion. https://api.sci.gov.in/supremecourt/2017/30325/30325_2017_13_1501_69248_Judgement_11-Mar-2026.pdf
• DoPT OM of 8 September 1993 gave 27% reservation in central civil posts and excluded the creamy layer through six categories. https://static.pib.gov.in/WriteReadData/specificdocs/documents/2023/may/doc2023519200401.pdf
• Mandal Commission was the second Backward Classes Commission, appointed under Article 340 (31 December 1979). https://api.sci.gov.in/supremecourt/2019/23618/23618_2019_35_1501_27992_Judgement_05-May-2021.pdf
• Creamy-layer income limit: Rs 1 lakh (1993), Rs 2.5 lakh (2004), then Rs 4.5 lakh by later revision. https://ncbc.nic.in/Writereaddata/1118.pdf
• EWS 10% quota rests on Articles 15(6) and 16(6) (103rd Amendment, 2019) and sits outside the 50% limit of Articles 15(4) and 16(4). https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=1985914
Mains Recall (CSE 2027):
• [Judgment] Indra Sawhney: non-exclusion of the creamy layer would violate Articles 14 and 16, so exclusion is a constitutional necessity. https://api.sci.gov.in/supremecourt/2017/30325/30325_2017_13_1501_69248_Judgement_11-Mar-2026.pdf
• [Judgment] Indra Sawhney directed criteria within four months; the Expert Committee centred them on social status, not income alone. https://api.sci.gov.in/supremecourt/2017/30325/30325_2017_13_1501_69248_Judgement_11-Mar-2026.pdf
• [Committee] NCBC supplementary report advised raising the creamy-layer limit from Rs 6 lakh to Rs 15 lakh, noting 27% OBC vacancies stayed unfilled. https://www.ncbc.nic.in/Writereaddata/Supplementary%20Creamy%20Layer%20Report%20241115%20final%20at%20430PM%20Corrected%20by%2005052016%20page%20no15635980433155122719.pdf
• [Data] OBC share in direct recruitment to central civil posts reached 34.52% in 2018 against the 27% quota. https://static.pib.gov.in/WriteReadData/specificdocs/documents/2023/may/doc2023519200401.pdf
• [Counterpoint] Sawhney held exclusion should not be merely economic; stringent income limits left quota posts unfilled. https://www.ncbc.nic.in/Writereaddata/Supplementary%20Creamy%20Layer%20Report%20241115%20final%20at%20430PM%20Corrected%20by%2005052016%20page%20no15635980433155122719.pdf
• [Way forward] Revise the limit periodically and keep exclusion rooted in social advancement, as Indra Sawhney and NCBC advised. https://www.ncbc.nic.in/Writereaddata/Supplementary%20Creamy%20Layer%20Report%20241115%20final%20at%20430PM%20Corrected%20by%2005052016%20page%20no15635980433155122719.pdf

[Prelims 2027] Which judgment introduced the creamy layer concept for OBC reservation, and which Article provides OBC reservation in public employment?

Syllabus Tag: GS3 › Science & Technology › IT, space, computers, robotics, nanotechnology, biotechnology, intellectual property rights › Satellite internet — Starlink security risks
CA Topic / Headline: An op-ed says Starlink suits remote settlements, borders and disaster areas but gives India limited control: it may stay usable where authorities order a switch-off; the ITU Board noted unauthorised Starlink transmissions in Iran in October 2026. Why it matters: satcom regulation, spectrum, space-law responsibility and security (GS3 S&T).
Prelims Recall (CSE 2027):
• Outer Space Treaty, 1967 Article II: outer space is not subject to national appropriation by claim of sovereignty, use or occupation. https://www.unoosa.org/unoosa/en/ourwork/spacelaw/treaties/outerspacetreaty.html
• Outer Space Treaty Article VI: States bear responsibility for national space activities, including private entities that need authorisation and continuing supervision. https://www.unoosa.org/unoosa/en/ourwork/spacelaw/treaties/outerspacetreaty.html
• Outer Space Treaty Article VIII: the State of registry retains jurisdiction and control over a launched object and its personnel. https://www.unoosa.org/pdf/pres/2010/SLW2010/02-02.pdf
• Telecommunications Act, 2023 section 4: Centre owns spectrum for the people; assignment is by auction except First Schedule entries, assigned administratively. https://www.trai.gov.in/sites/default/files/2025-05/Recommendtion_09052025.pdf
• DoT has issued GMPCS, NLD and ISP Category A authorisations for NGSO satellite services; spectrum terms were referred to TRAI. https://trai.gov.in/sites/default/files/2024-11/BIF_26102024.pdf
Mains Recall (CSE 2027):
• [Provision] Section 4 of the Telecommunications Act, 2023 makes auction the default and administrative assignment the exception for First Schedule entries. https://www.trai.gov.in/sites/default/files/2025-05/Recommendtion_09052025.pdf
• [Provision] Outer Space Treaty Article VI makes the home State supervise private operators, a template for authorising foreign constellations. https://www.unoosa.org/unoosa/en/ourwork/spacelaw/treaties/outerspacetreaty.html
• [Counterpoint] Industry (ISpA) argues satellite spectrum is shared and non-exclusive worldwide, and that auctions risk reciprocal action against Indian operators. https://www.trai.gov.in/sites/default/files/2024-11/ISpA_02062023.pdf
• [Way forward] Finalise TRAI's 2026 Satellite Communication Network authorisation framework under section 3(1)(b), which stakeholders link to Indian incorporation and IN-SPACe authorisation. https://trai.gov.in/sites/default/files/2026-05/ISpA_27052026.pdf

Syllabus Tag: GS2 › International Relations › Important international institutions, agencies and fora: structure, mandate › Slavery reparations — Jamaica reference to the JCPC
CA Topic / Headline: Jamaica asked Charles III to refer three legal questions on the lawfulness of enslaving Africans to the Judicial Committee of the Privy Council under the Judicial Committee Act 1833; the UK is open to an apology but rules out financial reparations. Why it matters: reparatory justice, international law and Commonwealth institutions (GS2 IR).
Prelims Recall (CSE 2027):
• CARICOM Ten Point Plan for Reparatory Justice (endorsed March 2014) seeks apology, repatriation, cultural institutions and debt cancellation. https://caricom.org/reparations-for-native-genocide-and-slavery/
• Durban Declaration (2001): slavery and the slave trade are a crime against humanity and should always have been so. https://www.un.org/en/durban-20-anniversary/background
• Caribbean Court of Justice was inaugurated at Port of Spain on 16 April 2005 with original jurisdiction under the Revised Treaty of Chaguaramas. https://ccj.org/wp-content/uploads/2022/09/Rajnauth-Lee_20160616.pdf
• CCJ appellate cases come from Barbados, Belize, Dominica, Guyana and Saint Lucia. https://ccj.org/about-the-ccj/who-we-are/
• Jamaica signed the CCJ Agreement in 2001 but does not send final appeals to the CCJ. https://ccj.org/wp-content/uploads/2022/08/Saunders_20220803-1.pdf
Mains Recall (CSE 2027):
• [Provision] Durban Declaration paragraph 34 notes some States apologised and paid reparation where appropriate for grave violations. https://www.ohchr.org/sites/default/files/Documents/Publications/Durban_text_en.pdf
• [Data] An estimated 25 to 30 million people were forcibly uprooted from Africa through enslavement and the slave trade. https://www.ohchr.org/sites/default/files/2024-12/reparatory-justice-african-descent-people-1-en.pdf
• [Example] UN experts recommend States consider CARICOM's ten-point plan as a guiding framework for reparatory justice. https://www.ohchr.org/sites/default/files/2024-12/reparatory-justice-african-descent-people-1-en.pdf
• [Counterpoint] Legal controversies persist, such as the intertemporal principle, though speakers argue crimes against humanity carry no limitation period. https://www.ohchr.org/sites/default/files/documents/hrbodies/hrcouncil/sessions-regular/session60/advance-version/a-hrc-60%2077-advanceeditedversion.pdf
• [Way forward] CERD General Recommendation 40 asks States for time-bound national action plans combining monetary, non-monetary and structural reparatory measures. https://www.ohchr.org/en/stories/2026/09/beyond-compensation-un-committee-sets-out-broader-vision-reparatory-justice

Syllabus Tag: GS2 › Social Justice › Social sector and services: health, education, human resources › Human development — Keralam at 70
CA Topic / Headline: An op-ed says Keralam, if a nation, would rank 75 on the Human Development Index, ahead of China and 55 ranks above India (130), with lower infant mortality than the US; 82% of its men have 10 years of schooling against 47% in Gujarat. • HDI goalposts: life expectancy 20-85 years, expected schooling 0-18, mean schooling 0-15, GNI per capita $100-75,000 (2021 PPP). https://hdr.undp.org/sites/default/files/2025_HDR/HDR25_Technical_Notes.pdf
• India's HDI was 0.685 in 2023, rank 130 of 193, in the medium category (high starts at 0.700). https://www.undp.org/india/press-releases/indias-human-development-continues-make-progress-ranks-130-out-193-countries

Mains Recall (CSE 2027):
• [Data] Kerala's life expectancy is 75 years against 70 nationally, maternal mortality 19 against 97, and infant mortality is single-digit. https://spb.kerala.gov.in/sites/default/files/2025-02/ER_2024EngVol%201.pdf

• [Way forward] Plan for ageing: Kerala's 60+ share was 11.8% (2011) and is expected above 20%, raising chronic-disease demand. https://spb.kerala.gov.in/sites/default/files/2021-02/KDR_02_21.pdf

Syllabus Tag: GS2 › Social Justice › Welfare schemes for vulnerable sections; mechanisms, laws, institutions and bodies for their protection › OBC creamy layer — salary and agricultural income
CA Topic / Headline: The Supreme Court order of 6 November reaffirms its 11 March 2026 ruling: parental salary or agricultural income alone cannot decide OBC creamy-layer status; post status and category matter under the 1993 OM. The Centre's two-year request was rejected and compliance extended by two months. Why it matters: reservation jurisprudence, Indra Sawhney and civil-services allocation.
Prelims Recall (CSE 2027):
• DoPT OM of 8 September 1993 fixed creamy-layer criteria; income from salaries or agricultural land is not clubbed under the income/wealth test. https://pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=1559061
• Creamy-layer income limit is ₹8 lakh a year, raised from ₹6 lakh, effective 1 September 2017. https://ncbc.nic.in/Writereaddata/DoPTOM08.06.2018.pdf
• Indra Sawhney (1992), a nine-judge bench, upheld 27% OBC reservation under Article 16(4), capped total reservation ordinarily at 50% and mandated creamy-layer exclusion. https://api.sci.gov.in/supremecourt/2017/30325/30325_2017_13_1501_69248_Judgement_11-Mar-2026.pdf
• Article 340 empowers the President to appoint a commission to investigate conditions of socially and educationally backward classes. https://www.constitutionofindia.net/articles/article-340-appointment-of-a-commission-to-investigate-the-conditions-of-backward-classes/
• Article 16(4) permits reservation in State posts for any backward class not adequately represented in State services. https://www.indiacode.nic.in/bitstream/123456789/19150/1/constitution_of_india.pdf
Mains Recall (CSE 2027):
• [Judgment] M. Nagaraj (2006): the 50% ceiling, creamy layer and compelling reasons are constitutional requirements without which Article 16 equality would collapse. https://api.sci.gov.in/jonew/judis/44551.pdf
• [Committee] The Ram Nandan Prasad Expert Committee, accepted in toto, centred creamy-layer criteria on social status of positions rather than income alone. https://api.sci.gov.in/supremecourt/2017/30325/30325_2017_13_1501_69248_Judgement_11-Mar-2026.pdf
• [Provision] Article 16(4) enables reservation for backward classes, but the Constitution is silent on creamy layer, a judicial doctrine from Indra Sawhney. https://prsindia.org/files/bills_acts/bills_parliament/2004/scr1189070294_Scheduled_Castes__Scheduled_Tribes_and_Other_Backward_Classes_____Reservation_in_Posts_and_Services__Bill__2004.pdf
• [Data] NCBC's 2015 supplementary report noted OBCs had filled not more than 16% of the 27% quota. https://www.ncbc.nic.in/Writereaddata/Supplementary%20Creamy%20Layer%20Report%20241115%20final%20at%20430PM%20Corrected%20by%2005052016%20page%20no15635980433155122719.pdf
• [Counterpoint] A parliamentary committee felt creamy layer indirectly brings in the economic criteria the constitutional framers rejected. https://prsindia.org/files/bills_acts/bills_parliament/2004/scr1189070294_Scheduled_Castes__Scheduled_Tribes_and_Other_Backward_Classes_____Reservation_in_Posts_and_Services__Bill__2004.pdf
• [Way forward] Settle equivalence of PSU and private posts with government posts and revise the income criterion every three years, as the 1993 OM envisaged. https://pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=1559061
Relevance & Revision Note:
[Prelims 2027] Creamy layer: 1993 DoPT OM, ₹8 lakh limit, salary and agricultural income not clubbed, Indra Sawhney basis.
[Mains 2027] Examine how the creamy-layer test balances equity and inclusion within OBC reservation. (GS2, 15)
[Link] 2024 GS1 PYQ on affirmative action not reaching the underprivileged

Syllabus Tag: GS2 › Polity › Constitution: historical underpinnings, evolution, features, amendments, significant provisions, basic structure › Reservation ceiling and Ninth Schedule
CA Topic / Headline: Karnataka has moved the Supreme Court against the High Court's 12 October order quashing its hike in SC quota from 15% to 17% and ST from 3% to 7%, which took total reservation to 56%, above the 50% cap; the State seeks Ninth Schedule cover. Why it matters: 50% ceiling, Article 31B and judicial review.
Prelims Recall (CSE 2027):
• Article 31B protects laws placed in the Ninth Schedule from challenge as violating fundamental rights; the 76th Amendment (1994) added Tamil Nadu's 69% reservation Act. https://www.legislative.gov.in/static/uploads/2025/07/f3b4ae82cc697454c66a98b610225f34.pdf
• Indra Sawhney (16 November 1992) held total reservations under Article 16(4) should not exceed 50%. https://www.legislative.gov.in/static/uploads/2025/07/f3b4ae82cc697454c66a98b610225f34.pdf
• Article 16(4B), inserted by the 81st Amendment (2000), keeps carried-forward unfilled vacancies outside the 50% ceiling of the year they are filled. https://prsindia.org/files/bills_acts/bills_parliament/2004/scr1189070294_Scheduled_Castes__Scheduled_Tribes_and_Other_Backward_Classes_____Reservation_in_Posts_and_Services__Bill__2004.pdf
• Articles 15(6) and 16(6), inserted by the 103rd Amendment (2019), give EWS 10% reservation outside the 50% limit on Articles 15(4) and 16(4). https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleaseIframePage.aspx?PRID=1806158&reg=3&lang=2
• Maratha reservation case (5 May 2021): the Supreme Court held the 50% limit crossable only in extraordinary circumstances backed by quantifiable, contemporaneous data. https://api.sci.gov.in/supremecourt/2019/23618/23618_2019_35_1501_27992_Judgement_05-May-2021.pdf
Mains Recall (CSE 2027):
• [Judgment] Indra Sawhney (1992) fixed the 50% ceiling; the Maratha ruling (2021) refused to exceed it without extraordinary circumstances and data. https://api.sci.gov.in/supremecourt/2019/23618/23618_2019_35_1501_27992_Judgement_05-May-2021.pdf
• [Provision] Article 16(4) permits reservation for inadequately represented backward classes; Article 15(4) permits special provisions for SCs, STs and backward classes. https://www.indiacode.nic.in/bitstream/123456789/19150/1/constitution_of_india.pdf
• [Example] Tamil Nadu's 69% Act of 1994 was placed in the Ninth Schedule by the 76th Amendment to secure protection under Article 31B. https://www.legislative.gov.in/static/uploads/2025/07/f3b4ae82cc697454c66a98b610225f34.pdf
• [Data] Karnataka Act 1 of 2023 recites that the Government was satisfied of extraordinary circumstances to raise SC and ST quotas above 15% and 3%. https://www.indiacode.nic.in/bitstream/123456789/19594/1/01_of_2023_(e)_sc_&_st.pdf
• [Counterpoint] The Union told Parliament in 2021 it has no proposal to override the Indra Sawhney 50% limit, narrowing political routes to higher quotas. https://pib.gov.in/PressReleaseIframePage.aspx?PRID=1739434
• [Way forward] Gather quantifiable, contemporaneous data on backwardness and representation to justify any breach, as the Maratha reservation ruling requires. https://api.sci.gov.in/supremecourt/2019/23618/23618_2019_35_1501_27992_Judgement_05-May-2021.pdf
Relevance & Revision Note:
[Prelims 2027] Ninth Schedule, Article 31B, 50% ceiling and 76th Amendment (Tamil Nadu 69%): which statements are correct?
[Mains 2027] Can States breach the 50% reservation ceiling through the Ninth Schedule? Discuss. (GS2, 15)
[Link] 2018 and 2019 PYQs on the Ninth Schedule

Syllabus Tag: GS2 › Polity › Functions and responsibilities of Union and States; federal structure; devolution of powers and finances up to local levels › Ladakh hill councils — LAHDC polls and Sixth Schedule demand
CA Topic / Headline: Ladakh's Chief Electoral Officer has barred protests within Leh and Kargil municipal limits, citing the Model Code of Conduct, ahead of multi-tier elections between 21 November and 4 December; LAB leaders had sought postponement. Why it matters: Sixth Schedule demand, Model Code and local self-government in Ladakh.
Prelims Recall (CSE 2027):
• Sixth Schedule (Articles 244(2) and 275(1)) lists ten tribal areas: Assam 3, Meghalaya 3, Tripura 1, Mizoram 3, each an autonomous district. https://prsindia.org/billtrack/prs-products/prs-standing-committee-report-summary-3175
• A Sixth Schedule District Council has at most 30 members: up to four nominated by the Governor, the rest elected on adult suffrage. https://www.constitutionofindia.net/schedules/provisions-as-to-the-administration-of-tribal-areas-in-the-states-of-assam-meghalaya-tripura-and-mizoram/
• The Bardoloi Committee drafted the Sixth Schedule to protect tribal areas and customs while enabling their development. https://prsindia.org/files/bills_acts/bills_parliament/2007/legis1223890886_The_Constitution__One_Hundred_and_Seventh_Amendment__Bill__2007_0.pdf
• Ladakh Autonomous Hill Development Council Act, 1997 (Act XXXI of 1997) provides for hill councils and an Inter-District Advisory Council. https://www.indiacode.nic.in/handle/123456789/5859?view_type=browse
• Leh's hill council began in 1995 on the Darjeeling pattern; Kargil's followed in July 2003. https://kargil.nic.in/lahdc/
Mains Recall (CSE 2027):
• [Provision] Sixth Schedule councils may levy land revenue and taxes and regulate money-lending and trading by non-tribals. https://www.constitutionofindia.net/schedules/provisions-as-to-the-administration-of-tribal-areas-in-the-states-of-assam-meghalaya-tripura-and-mizoram/
• [Committee] Ramachandran Committee recommended stating the minimum powers of District Councils in the Constitution, since devolved powers differ. https://prsindia.org/files/bills_acts/bills_parliament/2007/legis1223890886_The_Constitution__One_Hundred_and_Seventh_Amendment__Bill__2007_0.pdf
• [Scheme] 125th Amendment Bill, 2019 proposed larger councils, village and municipal councils and wider law-making powers for Sixth Schedule councils. https://prsindia.org/billtrack/prs-products/prs-standing-committee-report-summary-3175
• [Counterpoint] Autonomy is conditional: council regulations need the Governor's approval, and the Governor may assume council functions if administration fails. https://www.constitutionofindia.net/schedules/provisions-as-to-the-administration-of-tribal-areas-in-the-states-of-assam-meghalaya-tripura-and-mizoram/
• [Way forward] Legislate minimum devolved powers and village and municipal tiers, as the 125th Amendment Bill proposed. https://prsindia.org/billtrack/the-constitution-one-hundred-and-twenty-fifth-amendment-bill-2019
Relevance & Revision Note:
[Prelims 2027] Sixth Schedule: Articles 244(2) and 275(1), District Council size, Bardoloi Committee; LAHDC Act 1997.
[Mains 2027] Does the Model Code of Conduct justify curbs on protest during elections? Discuss. (GS2, 15)
[Link] 2015 Prelims PYQ on Fifth and Sixth Schedules; 2022 Mains PYQ on ECI and the Model Code

Syllabus Tag: GS3 › Environment › Conservation, environmental pollution and degradation, environmental impact assessment › Air pollution — CPCB plans to capture peak PM levels
CA Topic / Headline: CSE finds the week before Deepavali averaged PM2.5 of 236 µg/m3, 97% above 2025's 120 and 32% above 2024's 179; experts urge CPCB to stop capping readings at 1,000 µg/m3 and publish actual peaks. Why it matters: NCAP, GRAP and monitoring transparency (GS3 Environment).
Prelims Recall (CSE 2027):
• CPCB is a statutory body under the Water Act, 1974 with powers and functions under the Air (Prevention and Control of Pollution) Act, 1981. https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2307658&reg=48&lang=2
• National AQI has six categories (Good to Severe) built from eight pollutants; the worst sub-index decides the AQI. https://www.pib.gov.in/newsite/printrelease.aspx?relid=110654&reg=48&lang=2
• NCAP (January 2019) covers 131 cities; target is up to 40% PM10 reduction or the 60 microgram per cubic metre standard by 2025-26. https://www.pib.gov.in/Pressreleaseshare.aspx?PRID=1909910
• A non-attainment city exceeds NAAQS for five consecutive years and has at least three monitoring stations. https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=1983680&reg=48&lang=2
• GRAP was notified in January 2017 on CPCB's recommendation; CAQM, constituted in 2021, now publishes the revised GRAP. https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleaseIframePage.aspx?PRID=1989207
Mains Recall (CSE 2027):
• [Provision] Air Act, 1981 section 16: CPCB advises the Centre and plans a nation-wide programme for prevention, control and abatement of air pollution. https://www.indiacode.nic.in/bitstream/123456789/7781/1/air_act-1981.pdf
• [Data] NCAP: 95 of 131 cities improved annual PM10 in 2023-24 against 2017-18, and 18 met the PM10 standard. https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2036732&reg=48&lang=2
• [Scheme] NCAP earmarked Rs 19,614.44 crore for 131 cities (2019-20 to 2025-26): 49 via the XV Finance Commission grant, 82 via MoEFCC. https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2036732&reg=48&lang=2
• [Counterpoint] Implementation lags: by December 2023, Rs 9,650 crore was released to NCAP cities but about Rs 5,835 crore utilised. https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleaseIframePage.aspx?PRID=1989207
• [Way forward] Track city action plans on the PRANA portal and keep grants performance-based on measured PM10 reductions. https://static.pib.gov.in/WriteReadData/specificdocs/documents/2024/sep/doc2024924400701.pdf
Relevance & Revision Note:
[Prelims 2027] National AQI categories and pollutants; CPCB statutory basis; NCAP target and non-attainment cities.
[Mains 2027] Evaluate NCAP's progress and the role of data transparency in urban air governance. (GS3, 15)
[Link] 2016 Prelims PYQ on AQI pollutants; 2021 Mains PYQ on WHO AQGs and NCAP

Syllabus Tag: GS3 › Economy › Indian economy: planning, mobilisation of resources, growth, development and employment › Digital payments — UPI merchant discount rate
CA Topic / Headline: NPCI is yet to notify a date for the Merchant Discount Rate on UPI transactions, saying there is no update 'at the moment'. The Payment and Settlement Systems Act was amended in August 2026 and a 0.4% rate above ₹2,000 on merchant payments was clarified. Why it matters: digital payments, Section 10A and UPI sustainability.
Prelims Recall (CSE 2027):
• MDR is a fee merchants pay payment processors on card or UPI transactions, typically a percentage of transaction value. https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2114335&reg=48&lang=2
• From January 2020, zero MDR on RuPay debit and BHIM-UPI came through Section 10A of the PSS Act, 2007 and Section 269SU, Income-tax Act. https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2114335&reg=48&lang=2
• NPCI clarified MDR of 0.4% on UPI P2M transactions above ₹2,000, capped at ₹300 for transactions of ₹75,000 and above. https://prsindia.org/policy/monthly-policy-review/september-2026
• All person-to-person UPI transactions stay free; small merchants receiving up to ₹1 lakh a month through QR keep zero MDR. https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2310586&reg=48&lang=1
• Cabinet's FY 2024-25 incentive scheme pays 0.15% on UPI P2M transactions up to ₹2,000 for small merchants. https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2114335&reg=48&lang=2
Mains Recall (CSE 2027):
• [Provision] The August 2026 PSS Act amendment lets the Centre notify payment modes on which no charge can be levied; UPI up to ₹2,000 is notified. https://prsindia.org/policy/monthly-policy-review/september-2026
• [Scheme] A ₹1,500 crore incentive scheme (FY 2024-25) supports low-value BHIM-UPI P2M transactions and compensates acquiring banks. https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2114335&reg=48&lang=2
• [Data] MDR will apply to about 4% of merchant transactions; 5% of MDR collections will fund small-merchant UPI adoption. https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2310586&reg=48&lang=1
• [Counterpoint] Government says MDR is not a tax and customers do not pay it, yet banks must stop merchants passing it on. https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2310586&reg=48&lang=1
• [Way forward] Keep thin-margin sectors on the flat ₹5 charge and ring-fence the small-merchant fund so zero-MDR coverage and adoption continue. https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2310586&reg=48&lang=1
Relevance & Revision Note:
[Prelims 2027] MDR definition, Section 10A PSS Act 2007, zero-MDR since 2020, UPI P2M versus P2P.
[Mains 2027] Should UPI merchant payments carry MDR? Analyse sustainability versus financial inclusion. (GS3, 15)
[Link] 2018 Prelims PYQ on Merchant Discount Rate; 2017 and 2018 PYQs on UPI and BHIM

Syllabus Tag: GS2 › Polity › Functions and responsibilities of Union and States; federal structure; devolution of powers and finances up to local levels › Cooperative societies — Part IXB and nominated directors
CA Topic / Headline: An editorial flags Maharashtra's cooperative societies ordinance, promulgated 6 November, letting the government nominate five directors to large cooperatives, four with votes. At Gokul Dairy, where a Congress-led panel won 13 of 25 elected seats, four nominees helped the BJP side win 16-13. Why it matters: Part IXB, democratic control and cooperative federalism.
Prelims Recall (CSE 2027):
• 97th Amendment inserted Part IXB (Articles 243ZH–243ZT) and Article 43B, and made forming cooperatives a fundamental right under Article 19. https://api.sci.gov.in/supremecourt/2019/25060/25060_2019_1_302_39208_Judgement_18-Oct-2022.pdf
• Article 243ZJ: a board has at most 21 directors and a five-year term; co-opted members have no vote. https://api.sci.gov.in/supremecourt/2013/21321/21321_2013_32_1501_28728_Judgement_20-Jul-2021.pdf
• Article 243ZL: no board may be superseded or suspended beyond six months; one year for non-multi-State banking cooperatives. https://www.constitutionofindia.net/articles/article-243zl-supersession-and-suspension-of-board-and-interim-management/
• Union of India v. Rajendra N. Shah (2021): Part IXB held operative only for multi-State societies and Union territories, not State societies. https://api.sci.gov.in/supremecourt/2019/25060/25060_2019_1_302_39208_Judgement_18-Oct-2022.pdf
• Ministry of Cooperation is the nodal Centre ministry; Article 243ZR applies Part IXB to multi-State societies, reading State as Centre. https://www.cooperation.gov.in/sites/default/files/2022-12/Part-IXB-The-Cooperative-Societies.pdf
Mains Recall (CSE 2027):
• [Judgment] Rajendra N. Shah (2021): 'co-operative societies' is State List Entry 32, and Part IXB lacked ratification by half the States for State societies. https://api.sci.gov.in/supremecourt/2013/21321/21321_2013_32_1501_28728_Judgement_20-Jul-2021.pdf
• [Provision] Article 243ZI lets State legislatures regulate cooperatives on voluntary formation, democratic member-control, member-economic participation and autonomous functioning. https://www.cooperation.gov.in/sites/default/files/2022-12/Part-IXB-The-Cooperative-Societies.pdf
• [Counterpoint] Article 243ZJ denies co-opted members a vote, so voting nominees sit uneasily with democratic member-control. https://api.sci.gov.in/supremecourt/2013/21321/21321_2013_32_1501_28728_Judgement_20-Jul-2021.pdf
• [Committee] The Joint Committee on the Multi-State Cooperative Societies (Amendment) Bill 2022 aligned the Act with the 97th Amendment, including SC/ST and women board seats. https://prsindia.org/files/bills_acts/bills_parliament/2022/Joint_Committee_Report_on_the_Multi-State_Co-operative_Societies_(Amendment)_Bill_2022.pdf
• [Way forward] Align State laws with Part IXB: elections by an independent authority, fixed terms and limited supersession. https://www.cooperation.gov.in/sites/default/files/2022-12/Part-IXB-The-Cooperative-Societies.pdf
Relevance & Revision Note:
[Prelims 2027] 97th Amendment, Part IXB, Article 243ZJ board limits, 243ZL supersession, Article 43B.
[Mains 2027] Do government-nominated directors undermine democratic member-control in cooperatives? (GS2, 15)
[Link] 2015 Mains PYQ on cooperative federalism; 2021 Prelims PYQ on Urban Cooperative Banks

Syllabus Tag: GS3 › Internal Security › Communication networks, media and social networking, cyber security, money-laundering › Sahyog portal and Section 69A blocking
CA Topic / Headline: An op-ed says the Sahyog portal gives platforms three hours to comply with takedown requests, with nearly 1.95 lakh blocking orders sent to Instagram, Facebook and YouTube between March and July. It argues this departs from Shreya Singhal's Section 69A safeguards; MeitY also asked Meta on 10 October to review content ranking. Why it matters: free speech and intermediary liability.
Prelims Recall (CSE 2027):
• Section 69A, IT Act 2000 lets the Centre direct blocking of information in the interest of sovereignty, defence, State security, foreign relations or public order. https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2083249&reg=48&lang=2
• Blocking Rules 2009 (27 October 2009): a Designated Officer not below Joint Secretary issues directions after a committee examines the request. https://upload.indiacode.nic.in/showfile?actid=AC_CEN_45_76_00001_200021_1517807324077&filename=blocking_for_access_of_information_rule_2009.pdf&type=rule
• Shreya Singhal (24 March 2015) held Section 69A and the 2009 Blocking Rules constitutionally valid, calling it narrowly drawn with safeguards. https://digiscr.sci.gov.in/view_judgment?id=OTMwMQ%3D%3D
• Sahyog portal, run by the Indian Cyber Crime Coordination Centre (I4C), sends takedown notices to intermediaries under Section 79(3)(b). https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2298330&reg=1&lang=1
• I4C has blocked over 2,77,053 illegal apps, websites, accounts and links through Sahyog and proactive intimation to intermediaries. https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2298330&reg=1&lang=1
Mains Recall (CSE 2027):
• [Provision] Under the 69A Rules, the IT Secretary blocks on a Joint Secretary-level committee's recommendation, and the originator gets a hearing. https://prsindia.org/billtrack/amendments-to-it-rules-2021
• [Judgment] Shreya Singhal (2015): intermediaries disable content only on a court or government order; Section 69A survived as narrowly drawn. https://prsindia.org/billtrack/amendments-to-it-rules-2021
• [Data] I4C has blocked over 2,77,053 illegal apps, websites, accounts and links through Sahyog and proactive action. https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2298330&reg=1&lang=1
• [Counterpoint] Sahyog notices rest on Section 79(3)(b), a separate route from Section 69A's committee-reviewed blocking orders. https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleseDetailm.aspx?PRID=2154268&reg=48&lang=2
• [Way forward] Publish blocking and takedown data and ensure originators get a hearing, as the 69A Rules provide, to meet Shreya Singhal safeguards. https://prsindia.org/billtrack/amendments-to-it-rules-2021
Relevance & Revision Note:
[Prelims 2027] Section 69A, Blocking Rules 2009, Section 79(3)(b), I4C and Sahyog portal.
[Mains 2027] Do takedown portals meet Shreya Singhal safeguards on free speech? Critically examine. (GS3, 15)
[Link] first appearance — no PYQ yet

Syllabus Tag: GS3 › Economy › Inclusive growth and issues arising from it › Credit guarantee — CGFMU and PMMY
CA Topic / Headline: Cabinet extended the Credit Guarantee Fund for Micro Units by five years to March 2031. CGFMU has been a catalyst for growth of Pradhan Mantri Mudra Yojana loans, which stand at ₹43.34 lakh crore across 60.36 crore loans till September 2026. Why it matters: MSME credit, financial inclusion and PMMY.
Prelims Recall (CSE 2027):
• CGFMU was set up in January 2016 under National Credit Guarantee Trustee Company (NCGTC), a wholly owned Government of India company. https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=1914739&reg=3&lang=2
• PMMY, launched 8 April 2015, gives collateral-free loans to non-farm micro enterprises through banks, NBFCs and MFIs. https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=1945004
• PMMY categories: Shishu up to ₹50,000; Kishor to ₹5 lakh; Tarun to ₹10 lakh; Tarun Plus to ₹20 lakh. https://www.financialservices.gov.in/pradhan-mantri-mudra-yojana-pmmy
• Tarun Plus, effective 24 October 2024, is for entrepreneurs who repaid Tarun loans; CGFMU covers PMMY loans up to ₹20 lakh. https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleaseIframePage.aspx?PRID=2068019&reg=48&lang=2
• From FY 2020-21, SHG loans of ₹10–20 lakh also qualify for CGFMU cover. https://financialservices.gov.in/sites/default/files/2026-05/DFS-ANNUAL-REPORT-ENGLISH-2025-26.pdf
Mains Recall (CSE 2027):
• [Data] Under PMMY, ₹33.65 lakh crore was sanctioned by March 2025; Shishu was 78% of loans but 35% of the amount. https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2119954
• [Provision] CGFMU guarantees PMMY loans by lending institutions, reducing credit risk and enabling collateral-free credit to micro enterprises. https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2249942&reg=48&lang=2
• [Scheme] A 2% interest subvention on Shishu loans for 12 months (FY 2020-21) eased borrower credit costs under Aatmanirbhar Bharat. https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2119954
• [Counterpoint] Larger loans remain thin: Tarun Plus was only 0.095% of the amount sanctioned. https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2249915&reg=3&lang=1
• [Way forward] Use CGFMU cover to move borrowers up the Shishu, Kishor, Tarun and Tarun Plus ladder as businesses grow. https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2249942&reg=48&lang=2
Relevance & Revision Note:
[Prelims 2027] CGFMU: set up January 2016, NCGTC trustee; PMMY categories Shishu, Kishor, Tarun, Tarun Plus.
[Mains 2027] Assess PMMY's contribution to financial inclusion and the limits of collateral-free credit. (GS3, 15)
[Link] 2016 Prelims PYQ on Pradhan Mantri MUDRA Yojana

Syllabus Tag: GS3 › Environment › Conservation, environmental pollution and degradation, environmental impact assessment › E-waste and battery recycling — black-mass export ban
CA Topic / Headline: DGFT has barred export of waste and scrap of cells and batteries containing lithium-ion black mass with immediate effect. An op-ed says recycling could meet about 10–12% of India's lithium demand for EV batteries, with over 8.7 million EVs on roads by FY 2025-26. Why it matters: critical minerals, EPR and the circular economy.
Prelims Recall (CSE 2027):
• Battery Waste Management Rules, 2022 (24 August 2022) cover EV, portable, automotive and industrial batteries on an EPR basis. https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2205804&reg=3&lang=1
• Producers must use a minimum share of domestically recycled materials in new batteries from FY 2027-28. https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2205804&reg=3&lang=1
• The rules prohibit landfilling and incineration of waste batteries; a centralised online EPR portal handles certificates. https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=1854433&reg=48&lang=2
• National Critical Mineral Mission runs to 2030-31 with a ₹16,300 crore outlay, covering 24 critical minerals including lithium and cobalt. https://prsindia.org/policy/monthly-policy-review/june-2025
• Ministry of Mines' ₹1,500 crore scheme incentivises extracting critical minerals from e-waste and spent lithium-ion batteries. https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2182108&reg=48&lang=2
Mains Recall (CSE 2027):
• [Provision] EPR makes producers responsible for collection, recycling and refurbishment; environmental compensation applies on shortfalls under the polluter pays principle. https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=1854433&reg=48&lang=2
• [Data] Producers procured EPR certificates for 7.29 lakh tonnes of battery metals against a 10.96 lakh tonne target. https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleseDetailm.aspx?PRID=2159301&reg=3&lang=2
• [Scheme] The ₹1,500 crore recycling scheme caps incentive at ₹50 crore for big and ₹25 crore for small recyclers. https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2182108&reg=48&lang=2
• [Data] Black-mass processing capacity is limited, so it was exported before extracting minerals; spent LIBs are about 60 kilotonnes a year. https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2182108&reg=48&lang=2
• [Counterpoint] Very few Indian players do end-to-end battery scrap to metal recycling, so an export ban can strain processing capacity. https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2182108&reg=48&lang=2
• [Way forward] Incentivise mineral extraction rather than black-mass production and formalise collection under EPR to retain critical minerals. https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2182108&reg=48&lang=2

Syllabus Tag: GS1 › Art & Culture › Indian culture: art forms, literature and architecture from ancient to modern times › Yuge Yugeen Bharat National Museum
CA Topic / Headline: The CCEA approved a ₹3,230 crore project for the Yuge Yugeen Bharat Museum in North and South Blocks, about 1,78,509 sq m, appraised by the Public Investment Board on 27 July 2026. Why it matters: heritage policy, Central Vista and museum governance.
Prelims Recall (CSE 2027):
• Yuge Yugeen Bharat National Museum will occupy North and South Blocks under the Central Vista Redevelopment Project, New Delhi. https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2114398&reg=3&lang=2
• The Prime Minister first announced the museum at the International Museum Expo in May 2023. https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleseDetailm.aspx?PRID=2086273
• India signed a technical cooperation agreement with France Museums Développement on 19 December 2024 for the museum. https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleaseIframePage.aspx?PRID=2114398&reg=3&lang=2
• The Government vacated North and South Blocks on 13 February 2026 for Seva Teerth and Kartavya Bhavans; the Cabinet made them museum space. https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2228026&reg=1&lang=1
• National Museum, established 1949 in New Delhi, houses around 2 lakh objects across 22 galleries; its current building opened in 1960. https://culture.gov.in/ministry/our-groups/museums
Mains Recall (CSE 2027):
• [Scheme] Ministry of Culture plans a museum showcasing over 10,000 years of civilisational journey through thematic, non-linear storytelling. https://culture.gov.in/ministry/our-groups/museums
• [Example] The France Museums Développement partnership covers a feasibility study, interpretive planning and building programming. https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleseDetailm.aspx?PRID=2086273
• [Data] PIB describes the museum as spread over 1,54,000 sq m and billed as the world's largest museum. https://pib.gov.in/PressReleaseIframePage.aspx?PRID=2040219&reg=3&lang=2
• [Counterpoint] Project timeline and budget were contingent on the feasibility study, leaving cost and heritage-conversion risks. https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleaseIframePage.aspx?PRID=2114398&reg=3&lang=2
• [Way forward] Use digitisation under the Google Arts & Culture MoU to give early public access while galleries are built. https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2333271&reg=48&lang=2

[Prelims 2027] Yuge Yugeen Bharat Museum: location, announcement, France Museums Développement, Ministry of Culture.

Syllabus Tag: GS2 › Governance › Government policies and interventions for development; issues in design and implementation › Swachh Survekshan 2025-26 and SBM-U 2.0
CA Topic / Headline: Navi Mumbai has been adjudged India's cleanest city in Swachh Survekshan 2025-26, with Surat second and Vijayawada third; Ujjain topped the 3–10 lakh category and Rewa the cleanest riverfront. Indore, cleanest for eight years, missed the top. Why it matters: SBM-U 2.0, urban governance and solid-waste management.
Prelims Recall (CSE 2027):
• SBM-Urban launched 2 October 2014; SBM-U 2.0 launched 1 October 2021 for five years. https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2147695
• Swachh Survekshan, conducted by MoHUA since 2016, is the annual survey ranking cities on cleanliness. https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2147695
• SBM-U 2.0 targets: all statutory towns ODF+, towns under 1 lakh ODF++, half of them Water+, all 3-star Garbage Free. https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=1694420&reg=3&lang=2
• Urban India was declared open defecation free in 2019; over 3,000 cities were ODF+ and over 950 ODF++ at SBM-U 2.0 launch. https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=1760039
• By April 2023, 14 cities including Indore, Surat, Navi Mumbai and Vijayawada were certified Water+. https://www.mohua.gov.in/static/uploads/2025/11/96ea39f2858e307ab94171e403161f25.pdf
Mains Recall (CSE 2027):
• [Scheme] SBM-U 2.0 aims at 100% source segregation, scientific waste management and remediation of all legacy dumpsites. https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2147695
• [Data] Of 4,910 ULBs, PIB records 4,314 ODF+, 1,973 ODF++ and 214 Water+. https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2147695
• [Example] The MoHUA Secretary cited Madhya Pradesh, Chhattisgarh, Telangana, Andhra Pradesh and Tamil Nadu as exemplary States in solid-waste management. https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleseDetailm.aspx?PRID=1938520
• [Counterpoint] The minister said all cities reaching 3-star Garbage Free status by 2026 needs accelerated efforts, signalling a gap between rankings and delivery. https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleseDetailm.aspx?PRID=1938520
• [Way forward] Stress source segregation, integration of the informal sector and operating EPRs to sustain gains beyond rankings. https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleseDetailm.aspx?PRID=1938520

[Prelims 2027] SBM-U launch dates, Swachh Survekshan since 2016, ODF+, ODF++, Water+, Garbage Free star rating.

Syllabus Tag: GS2 › Polity › Salient features of the Representation of People's Act › Electoral rolls — SIR, Form 7 deletions
CA Topic / Headline: Bengaluru SIR flagged 1,13,059 of 2,55,926 new enrolments (Forms 6 and 8) as untraceable; ECI caps 1,200 electors per polling station; Manipur draft rolls show 19.94 lakh electors; editorial calls SIR a technology failure. Why it matters: roll integrity, Article 324, Section 21(3) RP Act 1950.
Prelims Recall (CSE 2027):
• Article 324 vests superintendence, direction and control of electoral rolls and elections in the Election Commission. https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleseDetailm.aspx?PRID=2139342&reg=3&lang=2
• Article 326: a citizen aged 18 or more on the qualifying date, not otherwise disqualified, is entitled to be registered as an elector. https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleseDetailm.aspx?PRID=2139342&reg=3&lang=2
• Section 21(3), RP Act 1950: ECI may, for reasons recorded, direct a special revision of the roll for any constituency or part of it. https://www.indiacode.nic.in/handle/123456789/1663?view_type=search
• SIR deletions fall under four heads: death, permanent shifting, duplicate entries, and electors found untraceable despite repeated visits. https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2289473&reg=48&lang=1
• After draft roll publication, claims and objections are filed through Forms 6, 7 and 8 before the final roll. https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2289473&reg=48&lang=1
Mains Recall (CSE 2027):
• [Provision] ECI anchors SIR in Article 324 and Section 21 RP Act; Article 327 makes Parliament's election law subject to the Constitution. https://api.sci.gov.in/supremecourt/2025/35785/35785_2025_1_1501_71617_Judgement_27-May-2026.pdf
• [Judgment] The Supreme Court (27 May 2026) held SIR within ECI's statutory mandate under Section 21(3) read with Article 324. https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2289473&reg=48&lang=1
• [Data] SIR ran in Bihar first (2025), then nine States and three UTs (Oct 2025-Apr 2026), then remaining States including Delhi. https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2289473&reg=48&lang=1
• [Provision] Safeguards: two to three BLO visits before untraceable status, draft roll publication, appeal to the District Magistrate then CEO, and BLA verification. https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2289473&reg=48&lang=1
• [Counterpoint] Petitioners argued Section 21(3) is constituency-specific, so a statewide special revision exceeds the provision. https://api.sci.gov.in/supremecourt/2025/35785/35785_2025_1_1501_71617_Judgement_27-May-2026.pdf
• [Way forward] Upload the documents behind each ERO decision to ECINET and publish deletion reasons so exclusions can be audited. https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleseDetailm.aspx?PRID=2139342&reg=3&lang=2
Relevance & Revision Note:
[Prelims 2027] Article 324, Article 326, Section 21(3) RP Act 1950; SIR deletion grounds; Forms 6, 7, 8.
[Mains 2027] Examine SIR's legality and its effect on electoral-roll integrity and voter inclusion. (GS2, 15)

Syllabus Tag: GS2 › Polity › Functions and responsibilities of Union and States; federal structure; devolution of powers and finances up to local levels › Delimitation — Article 82, seat freeze, Census
CA Topic / Headline: Special Parliament session on the Delimitation Bill, 2026 and a constitutional amendment (Lok Sabha up to 850 seats) needs 361 of 543 votes; the April 17 amendment attempt failed. Why it matters: Article 82, Women's Reservation Act 2023, federal seat shares.
Prelims Recall (CSE 2027):
• The 106th Amendment Act 2023 inserted Articles 330A and 332A reserving one-third of Lok Sabha and Assembly seats for women. https://prsindia.org/files/bills_acts/bills_parliament/2023/Constitution_106th_(A)_Act,%202023.pdf
• Women's reservation takes effect after delimitation based on the first Census after the 2023 commencement and lapses after fifteen years. https://prsindia.org/files/bills_acts/bills_parliament/2023/Constitution_106th_(A)_Act,%202023.pdf
• Articles 82 and 170 provide for readjustment of seats and constituencies after each Census by an authority Parliament decides. https://prsindia.org/billtrack/prs-products/prs-bill-summary-1776322465
• Seats reserved for women rotate after each delimitation, as Parliament determines by law. https://prsindia.org/files/bills_acts/bills_parliament/2023/Constitution_106th_(A)_Act,%202023.pdf
• The Delimitation Bill 2026 uses the latest published Census when the Commission is constituted, implying the 2011 Census. https://prsindia.org/billtrack/prs-products/prs-bill-summary-1776322465
Mains Recall (CSE 2027):
• [Provision] The 2026 amendment bill raises Lok Sabha from 543 to 850 seats (815 States, 35 UTs) and lets Parliament pick the Census. https://www.constitutionofindia.net/blog/union-proposes-overhaul-of-indias-electoral-framework-lok-sabha-to-expand-to-850-seats/
• [Provision] It keeps the 15-year women's reservation sunset, extendable by law, and extends reservation to Puducherry and Jammu and Kashmir assemblies. https://www.constitutionofindia.net/blog/union-proposes-overhaul-of-indias-electoral-framework-lok-sabha-to-expand-to-850-seats/
• [Data] The Bill reverts to seats proportional to population, so Lok Sabha constituencies across States have roughly equal population. https://prsindia.org/billtrack/prs-products/issues-for-consideration-1776322954
• [Counterpoint] PRS notes a simple-majority government could fix timing and Census basis, with no constitutional certainty on periodicity. https://prsindia.org/billtrack/prs-products/issues-for-consideration-1776322954
• [Way forward] Fix delimitation periodicity and Census basis in the Constitution and protect States' relative shares through consensus. https://prsindia.org/billtrack/prs-products/issues-for-consideration-1776322954
Relevance & Revision Note:
[Prelims 2027] Articles 82, 170, 330A, 332A; Delimitation Commission; 106th Amendment; 15-year sunset.
[Mains 2027] Does delinking delimitation from the Census threaten federal balance? Discuss. (GS2, 15)
[Link] 2026 Mains; 2024 and 2012 Prelims

Syllabus Tag: GS3 › Economy › Indian economy: planning, mobilisation of resources, growth, development and employment › Retail inflation — CPI 2024 series, 4% target
CA Topic / Headline: Retail inflation rose to 6.1% in October on the new CPI base 2024, with food and beverages at 8.5% and restaurants 10.1%; last above 6% in October 2024 (6.2%); repo rate 5.50%. Why it matters: breaches the RBI 4% ±2% band and narrows MPC room.
Prelims Recall (CSE 2027):
• The Centre, in consultation with RBI, notifies the CPI inflation target every five years under Section 45ZA of the RBI Act. https://www.pib.gov.in/newsite/PrintRelease.aspx?relid=148405&reg=48&lang=2
• The MPC has six members: three from RBI including the Governor as chair, and three appointed by the Centre via a search-cum-selection committee. https://www.pib.gov.in/newsite/PrintRelease.aspx?relid=148405&reg=48&lang=2
• Failure to meet the target means average inflation above 6% or below 2% for three consecutive quarters. https://www.pib.gov.in/newsite/PrintRelease.aspx?relid=148405&reg=48&lang=2
• New CPI has base 2024=100, weights from HCES 2023-24, and weighted items raised from 299 to 358. https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2291051&reg=48&lang=2
• The new CPI follows COICOP 2018 with 12 divisions; food and beverages weight is 36.75% in the combined index. https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2227012&reg=3&lang=1
Mains Recall (CSE 2027):
• [Provision] A band of 4% ±2% lets policy absorb short-term shocks while anchoring expectations at the centre of the range. https://www.pib.gov.in/newsite/PrintRelease.aspx?relid=148405&reg=48&lang=2
• [Data] Food and beverages remain the largest CPI component despite a lower weight, so food shocks still move headline inflation. https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2227012&reg=3&lang=1
• [Data] The new series samples 1,465 rural and 1,395 urban markets across 434 towns, widening coverage. https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2291051&reg=48&lang=2
• [Counterpoint] Supply-driven food spikes are outside MPC control; rate action works on demand, so the band tolerates temporary breaches. https://www.pib.gov.in/newsite/PrintRelease.aspx?relid=148405&reg=48&lang=2
• [Way forward] Combine calibrated MPC action with supply-side steps so expectations settle near 4%, not merely below 6%. https://www.pib.gov.in/newsite/PrintRelease.aspx?relid=148405&reg=48&lang=2
Relevance & Revision Note:
[Prelims 2027] Section 45ZA RBI Act; 4% ±2% band; MPC composition; CPI base 2024=100; COICOP 2018.
[Mains 2027] Analyse causes of persistent food inflation and the limits of monetary policy. (GS3, 15)

Syllabus Tag: GS3 › Internal Security › Security challenges in border areas; organised crime and terrorism › India-China border roads — ICBR-III, Arunachal Pradesh
CA Topic / Headline: ICBR-III plans 26 roads in Arunachal Pradesh after ICBR-I (2005, 27 roads) and ICBR-II (Sept 2020, 32 roads); ITBP has sanctions for suspension and log bridges. Why it matters: LAC connectivity, border infrastructure, China.
Prelims Recall (CSE 2027):
• India shares a 3,488 km border with China across J&K, Himachal Pradesh, Uttarakhand, Sikkim and Arunachal Pradesh; the LAC is not fully demarcated. https://www.mha.gov.in/sites/default/files/INDO_China_16022018.pdf
• 73 roads were identified as strategic Indo-China Border Roads; 61 were entrusted to the Border Roads Organisation (3,417.5 km). https://www.pib.gov.in/newsite/PrintRelease.aspx?relid=176947
• Under ICBR-I, MHA builds 27 roads in five States, executed by BRO, CPWD, NPCC and HP PWD. https://www.mha.gov.in/sites/default/files/INDO_China_16022018.pdf
• Delays arise from forest and wildlife clearance, hard rock, a short working season and land acquisition. https://www.pib.gov.in/Pressreleaseshare.aspx?PRID=1559104&reg=3&lang=2
• MoEFCC gave general approval under Section 2 of the Forest (Conservation) Act 1980 for border roads within 100 km aerial distance of the LAC. https://www.pib.gov.in/Pressreleaseshare.aspx?PRID=1540829&reg=48&lang=2
Mains Recall (CSE 2027):
• [Data] Arunachal Pradesh holds 27 of the 61 BRO-held ICBRs, totalling 1,791.96 km. https://www.pib.gov.in/newsite/PrintRelease.aspx?relid=137790&reg=3&lang=2
• [Scheme] The Border Area Development Programme funds roads, bridges, drinking water and health works in border areas, including along the Indo-China border. https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=1578949&reg=3&lang=2
• [Example] Outsourcing and enhanced financial powers for BRO executives were allowed to speed up border road works. https://www.pib.gov.in/newsite/PrintRelease.aspx?relid=137790&reg=3&lang=2
• [Counterpoint] ICBRs were planned for completion by 2012, yet many roads remain under construction, showing a long execution lag. https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=1515042&reg=48&lang=2
• [Way forward] Empowered Committees in border States, pre-cleared forest approvals and all-weather alignments can cut delay. https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=1515042&reg=48&lang=2
Relevance & Revision Note:
[Prelims 2027] ICBR scheme, BRO, LAC length 3,488 km, forest approval within 100 km of LAC.
[Mains 2027] How does border infrastructure shape India's China strategy? Evaluate delays. (GS3, 15)

Syllabus Tag: GS3 › Environment › Conservation, environmental pollution and degradation, environmental impact assessment › Siang Upper Multipurpose Project — Arunachal Pradesh
CA Topic / Headline: NHPC's Siang Upper Multipurpose Project (about 11,000-11,200 MW, 280-300 m dam, 9.2 bcm live storage) remains at pre-feasibility stage amid Adi protests, seen as a counter to China's Medog dam. Why it matters: Brahmaputra water security, EIA, tribal displacement.
Prelims Recall (CSE 2027):
• Upper Siang Project in Arunachal Pradesh is a declared National Project at pre-feasibility stage, planned for flood moderation. https://www.pib.gov.in/newsite/PrintRelease.aspx?relid=148367&reg=3&lang=2
• The Yarlung Tsangpo is the upper reach of the Brahmaputra; India demarched China on its mega dam on 30 December 2024. https://mea.gov.in/rajya-sabha.htm?dtl%2F38975%2FQUESTION+NO394+CHINAS+HYDROPOWER+PROJECT+AND+ITS+IMPACT+ON+INDIA=
• The India-China Expert Level Mechanism on trans-border rivers was established in 2006. https://mea.gov.in/rajya-sabha.htm?dtl%2F38975%2FQUESTION+NO394+CHINAS+HYDROPOWER+PROJECT+AND+ITS+IMPACT+ON+INDIA=
• India is a lower riparian State with established user rights over trans-border river waters. https://mea.gov.in/rajya-sabha.htm?dtl%2F38975%2FQUESTION+NO394+CHINAS+HYDROPOWER+PROJECT+AND+ITS+IMPACT+ON+INDIA=
• Central Water Commission was tasked with EIA studies for the Siang and Subansiri sub-basins, in consultation with CEA and MoEF. https://www.pib.gov.in/newsite/erelcontent.aspx?relid=67567&reg=48&lang=2
Mains Recall (CSE 2027):
• [Provision] The Inter-Ministerial Group (2009) recommended CWC-led EIA for Siang and Subansiri sub-basins covering downstream Assam impacts. https://www.pib.gov.in/newsite/erelcontent.aspx?relid=67567&reg=48&lang=2
• [Example] NHRC took suo motu cognizance of Siang protests (about 400 people at Beging village) over displacement and ecological fears. https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2133318&reg=48&lang=2
• [Counterpoint] Assam has raised concerns over cumulative downstream effects of hydropower in Arunachal Pradesh. https://www.pib.gov.in/newsite/erelcontent.aspx?relid=67567&reg=48&lang=2
• [Provision] India has urged transparency and consultation with downstream countries over China's mega dam. https://mea.gov.in/rajya-sabha.htm?dtl%2F38975%2FQUESTION+NO394+CHINAS+HYDROPOWER+PROJECT+AND+ITS+IMPACT+ON+INDIA=
• [Way forward] Complete a basin-wide cumulative EIA with local consent before DPR, and use the Expert Level Mechanism for data sharing. https://www.pib.gov.in/newsite/erelcontent.aspx?relid=67567&reg=48&lang=2
Relevance & Revision Note:
[Prelims 2027] Siang-Brahmaputra course, tributaries, Yarlung Tsangpo, Expert Level Mechanism 2006.
[Mains 2027] Discuss hydropower on Brahmaputra against ecological and downstream concerns. (GS3, 15)
