Syllabus Tag: GS2 › International Relations › India and its neighbourhood relations › India-Bangladesh — Hasina passport request and extradition
CA Topic / Headline: Bangladesh asked India, via its High Commission, for Sheikh Hasina's passport; extradition versus a prisoner-transfer route is debated, and the Ganga Water Treaty expires next month. Bangladesh PM is Tarique Rahman. Why it matters: neighbourhood policy, 2013 extradition treaty, water sharing.
Prelims Recall (CSE 2027):
• The Ganga Waters Treaty was signed on 12 December 1996 for lean-season sharing at Farakka. https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=1993077&reg=48&lang=2
• Sharing runs from 1 January to 31 May each year in ten-day periods; Farakka is the last control structure on the Ganga in India. https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=1993077&reg=48&lang=2
• The 1996 treaty is valid for 30 years with a provision to review after five years. https://www.pib.gov.in/newsite/PrintRelease.aspx?relid=67568&reg=3&lang=2
• A Joint Committee headed by Members of the Joint Rivers Commission monitors the sharing. https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=1993077&reg=48&lang=2
• India and Bangladesh have an extradition treaty (2013) in force; Article 6 lets a State refuse an offence of political character. https://www.mea.gov.in/Portal/LegalTreatiesDoc/BG13B1143.pdf
Mains Recall (CSE 2027):
• [Provision] Bangladesh sought Hasina's extradition for offences allegedly committed before she came to India on 5 August 2024. https://www.mea.gov.in/rajya-sabha.htm?dtl%2F38984%2FQUESTION+NO404+EXTRADITION+NOTICE=
• [Provision] The 2013 treaty allows refusal for political offences, with listed exclusions such as offences under multilateral treaties. https://www.mea.gov.in/Portal/LegalTreatiesDoc/BG13B1143.pdf
• [Data] India and Bangladesh share 54 common rivers; the Joint Rivers Commission is the key institution. https://www.mea.gov.in/images/pdf/india-bangladesh-relations-04-05-2012-press-release.pdf
• [Counterpoint] Without renewal, the treaty lapses after 30 years, leaving lean-season Farakka sharing without a legal anchor. https://www.pib.gov.in/newsite/PrintRelease.aspx?relid=67568&reg=3&lang=2
• [Way forward] Negotiate renewal through the Joint Rivers Commission and handle the extradition request via treaty channels. https://www.mea.gov.in/leta
Relevance & Revision Note:
[Prelims 2027] Ganga Treaty 1996 (30 years, Farakka, 1 Jan-31 May); 2013 extradition treaty; political offence clause.
[Mains 2027] Assess challenges to India-Bangladesh ties after the 2024 change in Dhaka. (GS2, 15)
[Link] 2013 Mains

Syllabus Tag: GS2 › Polity › Statutory, regulatory and quasi-judicial bodies › NHRC — Meta-UNICEF funding, child safety online
CA Topic / Headline: NHRC wrote to the Women and Child Development Ministry on Meta-UNICEF funding and child sexual abuse material (CSAM) concerns. Why it matters: online child protection and NHRC's statutory role under the Protection of Human Rights Act 1993.
Prelims Recall (CSE 2027):
• NHRC was established on 12 October 1993 under the Protection of Human Rights Act 1993, in line with the Paris Principles. https://nhrc.nic.in/assets/uploads/publication/NHRCbrochure.pdf
• The 2019 amendment lets a former Judge of the Supreme Court, not only a former CJI, chair the NHRC. https://www.pib.gov.in/pressreleaseiframepage.aspx?prid=1579522&reg=3&lang=2
• The amendment raised members from two to three (one woman) and cut the term of Chairperson and Members from five to three years. https://nhrc.nic.in/assets/uploads/annual_reports/AR_2019-2020_EN.pdf
• Chairpersons of seven bodies, including NCPCR and NCBC, are deemed Members of the NHRC. https://nhrc.nic.in/assets/uploads/annual_reports/AR_2019-2020_EN.pdf
• The President appoints on the recommendation of a committee chaired by the Prime Minister. https://nhrc.nic.in/assets/uploads/publication/NHRCbrochure.pdf
Mains Recall (CSE 2027):
• [Provision] The selection committee has the PM, Lok Sabha Speaker, Home Minister, both Leaders of Opposition and Rajya Sabha Deputy Chairman. https://nhrc.nic.in/assets/uploads/publication/NHRCbrochure.pdf
• [Data] NHRC has a Chairperson, five full-time Members and seven deemed Members. https://nhrc.nic.in/assets/uploads/publication/Overview%20of%20National%20Human%20Rights%20Commission,%20its%20functions%20and%20various%20activities.pdf
• [Provision] The Secretary-General exercises administrative and financial powers, except judicial functions, under the Chairperson's control. https://nhrc.nic.in/assets/uploads/publication/Overview%20of%20National%20Human%20Rights%20Commission,%20its%20functions%20and%20various%20activities.pdf
• [Counterpoint] A three-year term with reappointment may weaken security of tenure and independence from the executive. https://nhrc.nic.in/assets/uploads/annual_reports/AR_2019-2020_EN.pdf
• [Way forward] Strengthen Paris Principles compliance through pluralism and autonomy, as the 2019 amendment sought. https://www.pib.gov.in/pressreleaseiframepage.aspx?prid=1579522&reg=3&lang=2

Syllabus Tag: GS3 › Science & Technology › IT, space, computers, robotics, nanotechnology, biotechnology, intellectual property rights › PSLV — PS3 stage ground test
CA Topic / Headline: ISRO conducted a ground static test of the PSLV third stage (PS3) at Sriharikota. Why it matters: PSLV staging, HTPB solid propulsion and launch-vehicle reliability.
Prelims Recall (CSE 2027):
• PSLV is a four-stage vehicle with alternate solid and liquid stages. https://www.isro.gov.in/PSLV_CON.html
• PS1 uses the S139 solid booster with 139 tonnes of HTPB propellant. https://www.isro.gov.in/PSLV_CON.html
• PS2 is powered by the Vikas liquid engine using UDMH and N2O4. https://www.isro.gov.in/PSLV_CON.html
• PS3 is the third, penultimate stage and uses HTPB-based solid propellant. https://www.isro.gov.in/PSLV_CON.html
• PS4 is the final stage with two liquid engines burning MMH and MON. https://www.isro.gov.in/PSLV_CON.html
Mains Recall (CSE 2027):
• [Data] The PSLV-XL configuration is 44.4 m tall with a gross weight of 320 tonnes. https://www.isro.gov.in/PSLV_CON.html
• [Example] PSLV serves sun-synchronous, low Earth and geosynchronous transfer missions, earning the workhorse label. https://www.isro.gov.in/mission_PSLV_C15_CARTOSAT_2B.html?timeline=timeline
• [Provision] PS3's flex nozzle gives pitch and yaw control, while PS4 reaction control gives roll. https://www.isro.gov.in/mission_PSLV_C15_CARTOSAT_2B.html?timeline=timeline
• [Counterpoint] Solid stages cannot be throttled or restarted, so stage qualification before flight is critical to reliability. https://www.isro.gov.in/PSLV_CON.html
• [Way forward] Qualify stages through ground tests and widen industry production to sustain launch cadence. https://www.isro.gov.in/PSLV_CON.html

CA Topic / Headline: 22 bids were received for 10 GWh of grid-scale stationary storage under the ACC battery PLI scheme, which targets 50 GWh with a ₹18,100 crore outlay (Cabinet, May 2021). Why it matters: energy storage, import dependence, PLI effectiveness.

Syllabus Tag: GS3 › Environment › Conservation, environmental pollution and degradation, environmental impact assessment › Air pollution — GRAP, CAQM
CA Topic / Headline: Delhi air turned severe; stubble burning contributed 25.4% of PM2.5, students protested, and Section 163 BNSS orders were imposed. Why it matters: GRAP, CAQM and the Article 21 right to clean air.
Prelims Recall (CSE 2027):
• GRAP has four stages by Delhi AQI: I Poor 201-300, II Very Poor 301-400, III Severe 401-450, IV Severe+ above 450. https://caqm.nic.in/FileUploadDomain/WebsiteDocument/GRAP/GRAP%20Schedule/01fcdebf-83e1-4cfe-bc0c-d0b1470a4d4e.pdf
• Actions under a higher GRAP stage are in addition to those under lower stages. https://caqm.nic.in/FileUploadDomain/WebsiteDocument/GRAP/GRAP%20Schedule/01fcdebf-83e1-4cfe-bc0c-d0b1470a4d4e.pdf
• CAQM was constituted through an Act of Parliament passed on 13 August 2021. https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=1909910&reg=48&lang=2
• The Central Sector Scheme on Crop Residue Management has run since 2018-19; ₹4,090.84 crore was released till November 2025. https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2198748&reg=3&lang=2
• National Ambient Air Quality Standards were last revised in 2009 and are weaker than WHO guidelines for PM2.5. https://prsindia.org/policy/report-summaries/air-pollution-in-delhi-ncr-and-steps-taken-by-various-agencies-for-its-mitigation
Mains Recall (CSE 2027):
• [Judgment] The Supreme Court (Oct 2024) held every citizen has an Article 21 right to a pollution-free environment; compensation was recovered in only 473 of 1,084 Punjab stubble cases. https://api.sci.gov.in/supremecourt/1985/63998/63998_1985_6_7_56702_Order_23-Oct-2024.pdf
• [Committee] The Standing Committee (Dec 2025) urged revising NAAQS, fresh source apportionment and airshed-level planning. https://prsindia.org/policy/report-summaries/air-pollution-in-delhi-ncr-and-steps-taken-by-various-agencies-for-its-mitigation
• [Data] IITM-CDAC modelling puts non-local fire emissions at about 20% of post-monsoon PM2.5 in Delhi, rising to 50-75% in typical pollution events. https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=1808616&reg=48&lang=2
• [Example] CAQM directed mandatory 5-10% biomass co-firing in thermal plants within 300 km of Delhi. https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=1909910&reg=48&lang=2
• [Way forward] Shift to airshed-level enforcement across Delhi, Haryana, Uttar Pradesh and Rajasthan, with mechanised dust control. https://prsindia.org/policy/report-summaries/air-pollution-in-delhi-ncr-and-steps-taken-by-various-agencies-for-its-mitigation

Syllabus Tag: GS2 › Governance › Governance, transparency and accountability, e-governance, citizens charters, institutional measures › Sanction for prosecution — Prevention of Corruption Act 1988
CA Topic / Headline: Keralam's Governor sanctioned prosecution of ex-minister Abdurahiman in the Messi case, and the PMO sanctioned prosecution of two IAS officers in the ₹98.25-crore Tamil Nadu tender case. Why it matters: Section 19 and Section 17A of the Prevention of Corruption Act 1988.
Prelims Recall (CSE 2027):
• Section 19: no court takes cognizance of offences under sections 7, 11, 13 and 15 against a public servant without previous sanction. https://www.indiacode.nic.in/bitstream/123456789/1558/1/A1988-49.pdf
• The 2018 amendment asks the sanctioning authority to decide within three months, extendable by one month for legal consultation. https://api.sci.gov.in/supremecourt/2022/3264/3264_2022_15_1501_38812_Judgement_11-Oct-2022.pdf
• Section 17A (w.e.f. 26 July 2018) bars police inquiry into decision-related offences without prior approval. https://api.sci.gov.in/supremecourt/2018/40618/40618_2018_4_1501_67544_Judgement_13-Jan-2026.pdf
• No Section 17A approval is needed for arrest on the spot while accepting or attempting to accept an undue advantage. https://api.sci.gov.in/supremecourt/2018/40618/40618_2018_4_1501_67544_Judgement_13-Jan-2026.pdf
• The 2018 amendment extended sanction protection to persons who have ceased to hold the office. https://prsindia.org/files/bills_acts/bills_parliament/2013/Prevention%20of%20corruption%20as%20passed%20by%20both%20Houses.pdf
Mains Recall (CSE 2027):
• [Provision] The appointing authority is responsible for granting sanction, and must apply its own mind to the material placed before it. https://api.sci.gov.in/supremecourt/2022/3264/3264_2022_15_1501_38812_Judgement_11-Oct-2022.pdf
• [Judgment] The Supreme Court (13 Jan 2026) examined the constitutional validity of Section 17A. https://api.sci.gov.in/supremecourt/2018/40618/40618_2018_4_1501_67544_Judgement_13-Jan-2026.pdf
• [Data] Petitioners cited that prior approval was refused in 989 of 2,395 CBI cases (41.3%). https://api.sci.gov.in/supremecourt/2018/40618/40618_2018_4_1501_67544_Judgement_13-Jan-2026.pdf
• [Counterpoint] Sanction shields honest officials from vexatious prosecution, but delay and refusal can shield the corrupt. https://api.sci.gov.in/supremecourt/2022/3264/3264_2022_15_1501_38812_Judgement_11-Oct-2022.pdf
• [Way forward] Time-bound, reasoned and transparent sanction decisions with deemed-sanction or review mechanisms. https://api.sci.gov.in/supremecourt/2022/3264/3264_2022_15_1501_38812_Judgement_11-Oct-2022.pdf
Relevance & Revision Note:
[Prelims 2027] PC Act Section 19 sanction; Section 17A prior approval (2018); three-month timeline.
[Mains 2027] Does prior sanction protect honest officials or shield the corrupt? Discuss. (GS2, 15)

Syllabus Tag: GS2 › International Relations › Effect of policies and politics of developed and developing countries on India's interests; Indian diaspora › China — Taiwan reunification rhetoric
CA Topic / Headline: Xi Jinping reiterated peaceful reunification with Taiwan, citing one country, two systems and the one-China principle. Why it matters: Indo-Pacific security, India's one-China stance, UNGA Resolution 2758.
Prelims Recall (CSE 2027):
• UNGA Resolution 2758 (1971) recognised the PRC's representatives as the only lawful representatives of China to the UN. https://press.un.org/en/1997/19970917.ga9299.html
• India established diplomatic relations with the PRC on 1 April 1950, the first non-socialist bloc country to do so. https://www.mea.gov.in/Portal/ForeignRelation/India-china-072026.pdf
• The India-China Special Representatives mechanism began in 2003; the 24th round was held on 19 August 2025. https://www.mea.gov.in/Portal/ForeignRelation/India-china-072026.pdf
• The Kailash Mansarovar Yatra resumed in 2025 via Lipulekh and Nathu La after about five years. https://www.mea.gov.in/Portal/ForeignRelation/India-china-072026.pdf
• The 2006 India-China joint declaration records that India's one China policy remained unaltered. https://mea.gov.in/bilateral-documents.htm?dtl%2F6363%2FJoint+Declaration+by+the+Republic+of+India+an=
Mains Recall (CSE 2027):
• [Provision] India stated in 2006 it would continue to abide by its one China policy. https://mea.gov.in/bilateral-documents.htm?dtl%2F6363%2FJoint+Declaration+by+the+Republic+of+India+an=
• [Data] More than thirty India-China dialogue mechanisms exist across political, economic, cultural and consular matters. https://www.mea.gov.in/Portal/ForeignRelation/India-china-072026.pdf
• [Counterpoint] Taiwan's backers say Resolution 2758 settled only China's UN seat, not Taiwan's status or participation. https://press.un.org/en/1999/19990915.ga9593.doc.html
• [Counterpoint] Beijing says the resolution reaffirms one China and settles representation once and for all. https://press.un.org/en/1997/19970917.ga9299.html
• [Way forward] Keep the stated policy while deepening non-political economic and cultural links, and diversify supply chains from China. https://mea.gov.in/bilateral-documents.htm?dtl%2F6363%2FJoint+Declaration+by+the+Republic+of+India+an=
Relevance & Revision Note:
[Prelims 2027] UNGA Resolution 2758 (1971); India-China ties since 1 Apr 1950; SR talks 2003.

• The four boards: Under-Graduate and Post-Graduate Medical Education Boards, Medical Assessment and Rating Board, and Ethics and Medical Registration Board. https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=1659029&reg=48&lang=2
• The Post-Graduate Medical Education Board sets postgraduate standards and recognises postgraduate and super-speciality qualifications. https://prsindia.org/files/bills_acts/bills_parliament/2019/NMC%202019(1).pdf

• NEET gives one common entrance, with common counselling for postgraduate seats across institutions. https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=1581540&reg=3&lang=2

Syllabus Tag: GS2 › Polity › Constitution: historical underpinnings, evolution, features, amendments, significant provisions, basic structure › Preventive detention — NSA 1980, Article 22
CA Topic / Headline: NSA was invoked against Noida-protest activists, including theatre artiste Aakriti Chaudhary and journalist Satyam Verma; CaRWAN held a protest in Mumbai; the allegations are not independently verified. Why it matters: preventive detention, Article 22 safeguards, civil liberties.
Prelims Recall (CSE 2027):
• Under NSA 1980 the government must refer a detention order to the Advisory Board within three weeks. https://www.indiacode.nic.in/bitstream/123456789/1758/1/198065.pdf
• The Advisory Board reports within seven weeks of detention. https://www.indiacode.nic.in/bitstream/123456789/1758/1/198065.pdf
• The maximum period of detention under NSA is twelve months from the date of detention. https://www.indiacode.nic.in/bitstream/123456789/1758/1/198065.pdf
• Article 22(4): preventive detention beyond three months needs an Advisory Board of High Court judges reporting sufficient cause. https://www.constitutionofindia.net/articles/article-22-protection-against-arrest-and-detention-in-certain-cases/
• A detainee cannot appear through a legal practitioner before the Advisory Board. https://www.indiacode.nic.in/bitstream/123456789/1758/1/198065.pdf
Mains Recall (CSE 2027):
• [Provision] If the Advisory Board finds no sufficient cause, the government must revoke the order and release the person. https://www.indiacode.nic.in/bitstream/123456789/1758/1/198065.pdf
• [Judgment] The Supreme Court (29 Sep 2026) heard a challenge to an NSA detention alleging breach of Article 22 for grounds not furnished. https://api.sci.gov.in/supremecourt/2026/37437/37437_2026_6_1501_74756_Judgement_29-Sep-2026.pdf
• [Judgment] The Supreme Court (2024) warned that mechanical detention orders make the Advisory Board a vital safeguard. https://api.sci.gov.in/supremecourt/2024/8159/8159_2024_1_1501_51616_Judgement_21-Mar-2024.pdf
• [Counterpoint] The Act allows detention to prevent acts, not punish them, giving the executive wide satisfaction-based powers. https://api.sci.gov.in/supremecourt/2024/8159/8159_2024_1_1501_51616_Judgement_21-Mar-2024.pdf
• [Way forward] Insist on speedy furnishing of grounds, reasoned orders and effective Advisory Board scrutiny. https://api.sci.gov.in/supremecourt/2024/8159/8159_2024_1_1501_51616_Judgement_21-Mar-2024.pdf
Relevance & Revision Note:
[Prelims 2027] NSA 1980: Advisory Board within three weeks, 12-month maximum; Article 22(4).
[Mains 2027] Examine safeguards against misuse of preventive detention laws. (GS2, 15)
